name: Raleigh–Durham
lede: The Triangle's disc golf runs from the championship woods of Diavolo to the classic short course everyone learns on. We're publishing the region's best first.
introParagraphs: The Triangle's crown jewel is Diavolo at New Hope in Cary — a 22-hole championship course opened in 2020 with water holes and fusion pairs, already one of the most-loved courses in the region. Cedar Hills Rotary Park is the old-school wooded test from 1984, and Kentwood is the classic short course where generations of Raleigh players learned the game.
Apex Nature Park rounds out the top tier with its short, creek-crossed woodland loop. All four of our published Triangle courses are free.
New here? Kentwood to learn, Cedar Hills to test, Diavolo to be impressed.

faqs.question: How many disc golf courses are in the Raleigh–Durham area?
faqs.answer: Around 35 courses across the Triangle. We're publishing the best first — 4 are live today, with more added every week.

faqs.question: What's the best disc golf course in the Triangle?
faqs.answer: Diavolo at New Hope in Cary — the 22-hole championship course with water and fusion holes, opened in 2020 and already the region's favorite.

faqs.question: Are the Triangle's disc golf courses free?
faqs.answer: Yes — all four of our published courses (Diavolo, Kentwood, Cedar Hills, Apex Nature) are free to play.

faqs.question: What's the best beginner course in the Triangle?
faqs.answer: Kentwood — the short, friendly classic in Raleigh where most local players started. Apex Nature Park is another gentle option.
